_comment: Shared parser corpus for the architect stack. Both the Python splitter
(claude-bridge.mjs :: architectSignatureOf) implement the SAME rule: find the
top-level `:=` that starts the proof body. They are held to this one file so
the two implementations cannot drift — 'the same bug written twice in two
languages' is how every parser defect in this stack has arisen so far.
`sig` is the declaration signature (no body). `body` is the text after the
body-separating `:=`, or null when the declaration has none.

cases.lean: theorem t : 1 = 1 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: baseline — must not regress

cases.lean:
theorem t :
    let a : Nat := 3
    a = 3 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem t :
    let a : Nat := 3
    a = 3
cases.why: a let binder's := is top-level and comes first

cases.lean:
theorem enclosing_circle_radius :
    let k1 : ℚ := 1
    let k2 : ℚ := 1/2
    let k3 : ℚ := 1/3
    let R : ℚ := 6
    let k4 : ℚ := -1/R
    (k1 + k2 + k3 + k4)^2 = 2*(k1^2 + k2^2 + k3^2 + k4^2) := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem enclosing_circle_radius :
    let k1 : ℚ := 1
    let k2 : ℚ := 1/2
    let k3 : ℚ := 1/3
    let R : ℚ := 6
    let k4 : ℚ := -1/R
    (k1 + k2 + k3 + k4)^2 = 2*(k1^2 + k2^2 + k3^2 + k4^2)
cases.why: the live Leak Ultra failure: five binders before the body

cases.lean:
theorem t : let x := 3
  x = 3 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: binder without a type ascription still consumes one :=

cases.lean: theorem t : let x := 3; x = 3 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: semicolon form of let

cases.lean: theorem t : let ⟨a, b⟩ := (1, 2); a = 1 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: anonymous-constructor pattern: ⟨⟩ opens and closes before the :=

cases.lean:
theorem t : have h : Nat := 3
  h = 3 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem t : have h : Nat := 3
  h = 3
cases.why: have binds like let

cases.lean: theorem t : (let y := 2; y) = 2 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: a bracketed let is depth>0: neither counted nor its := consumed

cases.lean:
theorem t : (let a := 1; a) = 1 → let b := 2
  b = 2 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem t : (let a := 1; a) = 1 → let b := 2
  b = 2
cases.why: one bracketed let (ignored) plus one top-level let (counted)

cases.lean:
theorem t : let x : Nat := id (a := 1)
  x = 1 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem t : let x : Nat := id (a := 1)
  x = 1
cases.why: named argument := inside parens must not be mistaken for the body

cases.lean: theorem t (h : Nat := 3) : h = 3 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: optional-parameter default is bracketed

cases.lean: theorem t : ({ fst := 1, snd := 2 } : Nat × Nat).1 = 1 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem t : ({ fst := 1, snd := 2 } : Nat × Nat).1 = 1
cases.why: structure-instance := lives inside braces

cases.lean: theorem complete_x : deleted = complete ∧ letter = havoc := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem complete_x : deleted = complete ∧ letter = havoc
cases.why: 'let'/'have' as substrings of identifiers are not binders

cases.lean:
theorem t : P -- note x := y
    := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem t : P -- note x := y
cases.why: := inside a line comment is not the body

cases.lean: theorem t : P /- x := y -/ := by sorry_using []
cases.why: := inside a block comment is not the body

cases.lean: theorem t : P /- let q := 1 -/ = Q := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem t : P /- let q := 1 -/ = Q
cases.why: a commented-out binder must not be counted

cases.lean: theorem t : "a := b".length = 6 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: := inside a string literal is text, not syntax

cases.lean: theorem t : "let q := 1".length = 11 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: a binder keyword inside a string must not be counted

cases.lean: theorem t : "a -- b".length = 6 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: -- inside a string does not start a comment

cases.lean: theorem t : "a \" := b".length = 8 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: escaped quote does not close the literal

cases.lean: theorem t : 1 = 1 := rfl
cases.why: term-mode proof; the old bridge regex only knew `by`/`sorry`

cases.lean: theorem t : P → P := fun h => h
cases.why: fun uses => not :=, so the body := is still the separator

cases.lean: theorem t : P := sorry
cases.why: placeholder body

cases.lean:
theorem t : 1 = 1 := by
  let x := 2
  rfl
cases.why: binders inside the BODY are past the split and must not affect it

cases.lean:
theorem t : 1 = 1 := by
  have h : Nat := 2
  rfl
cases.why: same, for have

cases.lean: theorem t : 1 = 1
cases.why: signature only — nothing to split

cases.lean: lemma t : 1 = 1 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: lemma is interchangeable with theorem

cases.lean: theorem t : ∀ n : ℕ, n = n := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem t : ∀ n : ℕ, n = n
cases.why: unicode binders and types

cases.lean: theorem t {α : Type} [inst : Inhabited α] (a : α) : a = a := by sorry_using []
cases.sig: theorem t {α : Type} [inst : Inhabited α] (a : α) : a = a
cases.why: all three binder bracket kinds

cases.lean: theorem t : (n : ℕ) → (h : n = 0) → n = 0 := by sorry_using []
cases.why: colons inside the conclusion

cases.lean:
theorem t : let s := "x := y"
  s.length = 6 := by sorry_using []
cases.sig:
theorem t : let s := "x := y"
  s.length = 6
cases.why: binder counting and string skipping must compose
